rows.title: Homeowners are sitting on a record amount of equity, driving a shift toward more expensive homes, top economist says
rows.standfirst: “They are able to navigate these higher prices without as much of a ramification,” Realtor.com’s chief economist recently said.

rows.title: Cup Noodles instant ramen adds s’mores flavor—a bid to prove it’s ‘not just a boring thing you’d buy because you’re on a budget’
rows.standfirst: The packaged noodle brand is the latest to appeal to Gen Z’s eccentric taste for strange flavor combinations.

rows.title: Financial markets are pricing in more inflation under another Trump presidency—and bond yields are surging
rows.standfirst: The uptick in Treasury yields was led by the longest maturities, with 30-year bonds up more than eight basis points to 4.65%, the highest level since May 31.

rows.title: Fed Chair Jerome Powell says inflation is on the downswing—but don’t expect rate cuts yet
rows.standfirst: Fed officials still want to see annual price growth slow further toward their 2% target before cutting rates.

rows.title: The chief of Europe’s central bank is tired of people blaming Taylor Swift for the eurozone’s sticky inflation
rows.standfirst: “It’s not just Taylor Swift, you know,” Christine Lagarde told the ECB Forum. “Others have come as well.”

rows.title: Gen Zers and millennials have it harder than boomers did with college debt and buying a home—but they’re much better about saving
rows.standfirst: Gen Zers are saving even earlier than millennials, setting themselves up to become the most accomplished savers in history.

rows.title: We’re passing through ‘the worst housing affordability crisis’ ever seen, former Housing Secretary says—and it isn’t going to fix itself
rows.standfirst: Home prices rose at levels never seen before, and while the market is cooling down, housing costs are still beyond what people can afford, the Obama-era cabinet member said.

rows.title: 30-year mortgage rate climbs to just under 7%, pushing up borrowing costs for the first time since May
rows.standfirst: The uptick follows a four-week pullback in the average rate, which has mostly hovered around 7% this year.

rows.title: Wall Street’s biggest bear—once dubbed ‘Gandalf’ for his market foresight—is out of a job after predicting a U.S. recession that never happened
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan’s Marko Kolanovic made a name for himself as a contrarian during the pandemic, but too many wrong-footed calls finally caught up with him.

rows.title: If mortgage rates stay above 6.5%, ‘the chances of an imminent recovery are slim’ for housing demand, Capital Economics says
rows.standfirst: Mortgage applications and sales are weak, to say the least, off the back of dampening demand.

rows.title: Lumber prices are nearing all-time lows but could be headed for a rebound, executive says: ‘We are extremely, extremely cheap’
rows.standfirst: “Maybe we’ve started to recognize that this has finally capitulated and prices are ready to do something else.”

rows.title: Menopause stigma is impeding women’s career growth, survey says. Here’s how a lack of support is hampering ambition—and the economy
rows.standfirst: More than three in four women reported having no workplace accommodations for menopause.

rows.title: Morgan Stanley’s chief strategist Mike Wilson warns the stock market faces a 10% correction ahead of the U.S. election
rows.standfirst: The AI trade has lifted the stock market to all-time highs despite weakening economic data, prompting fears the upcoming Q2 earnings season could prove disappointing.

rows.title: Fed Chair Jerome Powell warns: Inflation isn’t ‘the only risk we face’
rows.standfirst: “Reducing policy restraint too late or too little could unduly weaken economic activity and employment,” he cautioned.

rows.title: There’s a wave of apartments coming, but building permits have plummeted almost 30% since the pandemic—and it could mean higher rents
rows.standfirst: “Property owners might start jacking up rents again once all of the new apartments hitting the market fill up with tenants and there’s no longer so much supply, which could be the case in a year or two,” a Redfin senior economist said.

rows.title: Wages in the U.K. are growing twice as fast as Europe and the U.S. thanks to one simple policy
rows.standfirst: Mandated increases in the National Living Wage is helping U.K. workers outpace pay rises in other major economies.

rows.title: Builders are pumping the brakes on new apartment construction—but landlords will keep ‘jacking up’ rental prices
rows.standfirst: Even though we’re “in a big hole” when it comes to housing supply, builders are backing off.

rows.title: Viral photo of $444 Trader Joe’s receipt sparks new debate over grocery inflation
rows.standfirst: Inflation hasn’t stopped stretching budgets.

rows.title: Top economist: Buyers and sellers should brace themselves for the 6% mortgage rate reality
rows.standfirst: Mortgage rates won’t be going back down to the historical lows seen throughout the pandemic, the National Association of Realtors’ chief economist said.

rows.title: Jerome Powell’s sudden bearishness on the jobs market is a welcome sign for Wall Street
rows.standfirst: “We’re not just an inflation-targeting central bank,” Powell told the House Financial Services Committee on the second of two days of semi-annual testimony to Congress. “We also have an employment mandate.”

rows.title: Inflation will go up regardless of who the next president is, but under Trump’s tariffs it would be higher for longer, Oxford Economics says
rows.standfirst: Jerome Powell is eyeing lower inflation, but Oxford Economics says it’ll rise after the presidential election—no matter who wins.

rows.title: Consumer prices drop for first time since 2022, giving hope rate cuts are coming
rows.standfirst: In a better-than-expected report from the government, consumer prices declined 0.1% from May to June after having remained flat the previous month.

rows.title: Investors scooped up close to 15% of homes sold in first quarter—‘a bigger piece of the pie than in any other’
rows.standfirst: But sales were way down, so the “pie was much smaller,” according to Realtor.com.

rows.title: The U.S. just got its best inflation report in over 3 years, but stocks are still down. Here’s why
rows.standfirst: “Is the market down? Or is this the most extreme rotation that we’ve ever seen out of everything that people have been hiding in?” Bancreek Capital Advisors’s Eric Pachman asked.

rows.title: President Biden steadfast on staying in the race. ‘I’m in this to complete the job I started.’
rows.standfirst: The president has faced growing calls from within his own party to stand down.

rows.title: Officials say food prices are dropping but shoppers aren’t buying it
rows.standfirst: The impending election may be leading some Americans to feel uncertain about the trajectory of the economy.

rows.title: Rents are reheating after flatlining for some time
rows.standfirst: “The months-long slowdown in the rental market appears to be leveling off as the busy summer season kicks off,” according to Zillow.

rows.title: Jamie Dimon: Prices will be higher for longer
rows.standfirst: The JPMorgan Chase CEO also warned that geopolitical instability could present future risks.

rows.title: Inflation becomes a wholesalers’ problem as producer prices surge
rows.standfirst: The Producer Price Index posted the largest one-month increase in over a year.

rows.title: Say goodbye to $6 Cheetos—snack companies finally lower prices
rows.standfirst: $6 for a bag of chips has consumers looking elsewhere, executives said.

rows.title: A sacred 13,000-year-old tree faces off with a California real-estate development
rows.standfirst: One of the world’s oldest living organisms is threatened by a new housing and industrial development in Riverside County.

rows.title: Bank profits slide as people struggle with debt
rows.standfirst: JPMorgan set aside $3.1 billion to cover potentially bad loans, up sharply from a year earlier, as delinquencies climb among some Americans.

rows.title: Three years ago houses in Sicilian villages were auctioned off for just €1. Now these regions have experienced a €100 million revival
rows.standfirst: Thanks to a boost from TV’s The White Lotus and a smart campaign from regional mayors, the future for Italy’s rural south has never looked brighter.

rows.title: Laurene Powell Jobs buys mansion on San Francisco’s Billionaire’s Row for $70 million, a record high for the city
rows.standfirst: The sellers of the San Francisco mansion bought the home in 2011 for $33 million.

rows.title: Janet Yellen is a fan of ‘Diners, Drive-ins and Dives,’ In-N-Out burgers, and visiting restaurants to go beyond economic data
rows.standfirst: “I certainly look at national data sets to understand what’s happening in the economy, but talking to people about what they’re experiencing is often really helpful in getting your mind around where people are coming from.”

rows.title: Mortgage rate waiting game means buyers gained more than $20,000 in purchasing power
rows.standfirst: On the back of last week’s inflation reading, mortgage rates dropped to their lowest level since early spring.

rows.title: Shrinkflation is hitting homes: Expect ‘the death of the hallway’ and other Tetris-like designs to cut construction costs
rows.standfirst: Architects and builders are avoiding “wasted” space in smaller home designs.

rows.title: Long periods of political violence are ‘very bad’ for the markets, analyst warns
rows.standfirst: The U.S.’s pivotal role in the global economy means that any negative effects from political violence would “spill over to the rest of the world.”

rows.title: Inflation is slowing at ‘a pretty good pace,’ Fed’s Powell says
rows.standfirst: The Fed chair suggested that inflation doesn’t need to drop all the way to 2% for the Fed to start cutting rates.

rows.title: Biden will propose a 5% cap on annual rent hikes amid housing affordability crisis
rows.standfirst: The plan to limit rent increases would only apply to landlords who own 50 or more units.

rows.title: Dublin residents are standing up to $2.3 trillion neighbor Google’s plans to build a pub, saying they are ‘effectively living’ on the tech giant’s campus
rows.standfirst: Locals living next to Google’s Dublin campus say they will be subjected to public urination if the tech giant is allowed to build a pub.

rows.title: Monthly housing payments have almost doubled in swing states since the last election
rows.standfirst: Swing states “have not been immune to the affordability crunch the country has been facing for the last several years,” Redfin’s senior economist said.

rows.title: Home prices are still sky-high, but the frenzied housing market is slowly coming down to Earth
rows.standfirst: In some ways the housing market is beginning to feel more like it did before the pandemic.

rows.title: Tesla let a man sell his Cybertruck because it didn’t fit in his garage
rows.standfirst: The man flipped his Cybertruck in a week for $2000 more than he paid for it.

rows.title: U.S. real estate is so expensive it’s even keeping out wealthy foreign homebuyers
rows.standfirst: Foreign buyers haven’t purchased so few homes since 2009—15 years ago.

rows.title: Former American Express CEO says business leaders are too scared to tell Trump what they really think of him: ‘They greatly fear there will be retribution’
rows.standfirst: After vowing to hit back at his political adversaries, CEOs worry they could be next if they anger Donald Trump.

rows.title: Pasta, steaks, and now chicka-chicka-boom-boom enchiladas. Olive Garden parent adds Tex-Mex to the menu
rows.standfirst: Chuy’s stock increased 5% today, but it’s year-to-date performance is down nearly 34%.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs top strategist: We’re on the precipice of a summer correction
rows.standfirst: The rising odds of Donald Trump winning the U.S. presidential election won’t be a positive catalyst, said tactical strategist Scott Rubner.

rows.title: The typical monthly housing payment just fell from an all-time high
rows.standfirst: In a rare bit of good news, mortgage rates are the lowest they’ve been in months.

rows.title: Renters finally get some good news as power begins to swing away from landlords
rows.standfirst: Rent on average is still more expensive than it was before the pandemic, though.

rows.title: Costco’s $80 ‘apocalypse bucket’ is packed with food that can last for 25 years
rows.standfirst: The bucket includes 150 meals with a total caloric content of 25,280, and is meant to help in “maintaining a sense of normalcy when the world around you might feel anything but normal.”

rows.title: A Fed interest rate cut won’t send mortgage rates plummeting, a top housing analyst says
rows.standfirst: Markets being what they are, “the simple act of the Fed cutting is not necessarily going to have a direct impact on mortgage rates,” Zelman & Associates’ Alan Ratner said.

rows.title: Gen Z is embracing ‘underconsumptioncore’ to fight climate change and inflation
rows.standfirst: “It just gets so tiring watching people tell me that this is the newest thing that I have to buy,” 27-year-old Adeline Um said.

rows.title: The Supreme Court’s ‘Chevron’ ruling is an existential threat to the ‘American economic miracle’ and will make the U.S. more like Europe, Lazard chair says
rows.standfirst: “By restricting the executive branch’s ability to craft and enforce regulations, the Supreme Court has opened the door to the Balkanization of the US economy.”

rows.title: Markets reassess ‘Trump Trade’ as Biden withdraws from race
rows.standfirst: “Investors should expect a spike in volatility,” said Dave Mazza, chief executive officer of Roundhill Financial, before Sunday’s announcement.

rows.title: Sovereign wealth investors think geopolitics and election uncertainty, not inflation, is their biggest risk
rows.standfirst: “Elections are a real unknown for the world economy,” said one Western central banker quoted in a survey from Invesco.

rows.title: Newly built homes are now cheaper than existing ones, and the discount is the greatest in 6 years
rows.standfirst: Before the pandemic, new homes were $15 to $22 more expensive than existing homes per square foot. In May, new homes were $3.50 cheaper than existing homes per square foot, according to Zillow.

rows.title: Kamala Harris went toe-to-toe with Jamie Dimon over a settlement for California homeowners. The big banks offered $4 billion—they settled at $20 billion
rows.standfirst: Harris took a big risk walking away from a national settlement in the aftermath of the Great Financial Crisis, and it could make the case for how she’ll deal with the corporate world if she’s elected president.

rows.title: The global M&A market’s big-deal bravado is losing steam as rates stay high in 2024
rows.standfirst: The largest sector for M&A globally was technology, with deal volume up 37% year on year, of which North America made up some 66% of the total.

rows.title: The Fortune 50 Best Places to Live will serve multigenerational families for the long haul
rows.standfirst: The third annual Best Places to Live for Families list is here.

rows.title: AI could be the best long-term disinflationary force in a challenging global economy
rows.standfirst: AI-driven efficiencies and even more sophisticated computing will drive the next 20 to 30 years of productivity gains.

rows.title: With homebuying ‘more expensive than ever,’ buyers are backing out of deals at a record pace
rows.standfirst: Last month saw more in-contract sales canceled than any June on record, according to Redfin.

rows.title: Florida is supposed to be a boomer paradise, but it didn’t even crack the top five best states for retirement
rows.standfirst: Billionaires like Jeff Bezos have resettled in Florida but other retirees have soured on the sunshine state

rows.title: Gen Z needs exposure to manufacturing careers as white-collar jobs look more prone to AI disruption—and student debt piles up
rows.standfirst: High schoolers should learn manufacturing technology basics and tour modern production plants, argues John Gardner.

rows.title: Downbeat CEOs worry inflation may prove stickier than anticipated after recent Fed disappointment
rows.standfirst: Fortune and Deloitte collaborated once more to take the pulse of the C-suite, and responses from CEOs surveyed in June reveal fresh concerns over pricing pressure.

rows.title: Private equity is devouring the economy as boomer entrepreneurs exit—but a new approach to employee ownership can change that
rows.standfirst: When the employees become owners under an ESOP roll-up, they can directly increase the value of their stock by sharing best practices across companies.

rows.title: Austin is the best place for renters, according to Realtor.com—forget the northeast or west
rows.standfirst: The top three metropolitan areas for renters are Austin, Oklahoma City, and Birmingham.

rows.title: 75-year-low: Federal minimum wage nears rock bottom
rows.standfirst: Raising the federal minimum wage appears to be a distant political reality. “You need to have the stars perfectly aligned.”

rows.title: Big Tech’s $1 trillion sell-off triggers worst day for stock markets since 2022
rows.standfirst: Excessive AI spending and geopolitical risks are prompting investors to cash in their chips.

rows.title: The ultrarich are scooping up mansions while almost no one else can afford a typical home
rows.standfirst: Luxury-home prices rose more than twice as fast as those of non-luxury homes, and still their sales jumped compared with typical homes, according to Redfin.

rows.title: Even September may be too late for a rate cut to swing the U.S. economy out of a recession, warns former Fed president
rows.standfirst: “Although it might already be too late to fend off a recession by cutting rates, dawdling now unnecessarily increases the risk.”

rows.title: Unilever customers swallowing ‘carryover pricing’ from historic inflation helped it generate $6.4 billion in profits so far this year
rows.standfirst: The Ben & Jerry’s owner says it’s starting to see negative pricing in some markets, but Europeans are still absorbing the group’s rising costs.

rows.title: Newsom’s call to sweep homeless encampments caught the eye of a Silicon Valley billionaire
rows.standfirst: But Vinod Khosla is dealing with his own housing woes, and has been for years.

rows.title: The worst streak of inflation in 4 decades looks like it’s finally nearing an end
rows.standfirst: Compared with a year earlier, the Fed’s preferred gauge of inflation declined to 2.5% from 2.6%.

rows.title: $1 million starter homes are more common than ever
rows.standfirst: The typical starter home is worth at least $1 million in 237 cities, up from 84 five years ago, Zillow said.

rows.title: Switzerland’s secret to beating inflation while the U.S. still struggles? Central Bank chief says it’s being ‘boring’
rows.standfirst: “It’s better to be called boring or stubborn than for people to say I’m pursuing the wrong monetary policy,” Thomas Jordan said.

rows.title: Wall Street is worrying about the ‘Sahm Rule,’ which predicts recessions—but its creator is not, yet
rows.standfirst: Claudia Sahm is cautioning against reading too much into her famous rule that suggests the U.S. is on the brink of a recession.

rows.title: One out of every 15 Americans is a millionaire, UBS says
rows.standfirst: The U.S. has 22 million people worth at least $1 million, according to UBS, about the same as Western Europe and China combined.

rows.title: Americans are cutting back on groceries to pay for AC
rows.standfirst: Sweltering summer heat has strained households so severely one-third of Americans are cutting grocery budgets and spending less on entertainment to cover cooling bills.

rows.title: There’s a ‘very low probability’ Trump or Harris will reappoint Jerome Powell as Fed chair, political strategist says
rows.standfirst: Powell’s dim prospects come despite the Fed chief nearing a huge win: the “softest of soft landings.”

rows.title: Today’s Fed meeting is merely a warm-up act for September, according to Wall Street
rows.standfirst: Wall Street analysts are not waiting to hear the outcome of today’s FOMC discussions. Instead, they want clues about Q3.

rows.title: Paris Saint-Denis and London Stratford tell a tale of two difficult suburbs transformed by the Olympic Games
rows.standfirst: ‘From my own experience with the 2012 London Olympics, the Games’ success is grounded in a long-term strategy focused on regeneration and investment.’

rows.title: Housing bust forecaster ‘Poison Ivy’ Zelman warns: Affordability grind isn’t going away anytime soon
rows.standfirst: While she sees further home-price deceleration and a dip in mortgage rates, Zelman says cost is the biggest risk to the housing market.

rows.title: Oil price surges after assassination of Hamas leader in Iran, sparking new fear of war and inflation
rows.standfirst: “It may get Netanyahu the war he’s been looking for,” warns foreign policy expert Trita Parsi.

rows.title: Inflation rears its ugly head in Europe, putting the European Central Bank in a fix—once again
rows.standfirst: An increase in the price of theater tickets, restaurant meals and hotel rooms threatens to derail the ECB’s expected rate cut in September.

rows.title: Columbia professor says McDonald’s can blame its sales woes on an election-stoked vibecession
rows.standfirst: The election is making people think the economy is worse than it really is.

rows.title: Fed keeps rates flat despite economists’ warnings it’s making a mistake
rows.standfirst: At a closely watched meeting, Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell hinted that a much-anticipated rate cut will happen this year.

rows.title: Gen Z and millennial homeownership rate plummets to 4-year low
rows.standfirst: But while the younger group saw their homeownership rate fall, some older generations saw theirs rise.

rows.title: Fed chair Powell says a rate cut is close, but we’re ‘not quite’ there yet
rows.standfirst: Over time, lower Fed rates should reduce borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, including mortgage and auto-loan rates.

rows.title: Black and minority farmers get $2 billion in payments after USDA acknowledges years of discrimination
rows.standfirst: USDA Secretary Tom Vilsack told reporters that the aid “is not compensation for anyone’s loss or the pain endured, but it is an acknowledgment by the department.”
